questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go to South Korea since I had been there before and wanted to experience the culture more in-depth and try living there for an extended period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
SKKU (Sungkyunkwan University) is very used to getting exchange students and therefore sends out all the information needed and explains everything very thouroghly.  It is all send in an acceptance package and it is also possible to google SKKU semester fact sheet to find some of the information already now. 

I had no problem trying to get into one of their dorms and registering for courses online since the information documents explained everything I needed to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university has a social club called hi-club which are local students who help exchange students on their semester abroad. In the beginning the explain all of the university's different systems and they also create events to meet other exchange students. 

I did not need that much help from the university upon arrival since I had figured everything out before the exchange with the help of their information documents. The few smaller questions I had during the exchange the university also helped me with without any problems.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I was at the Seoul (social science and humanities) campus. 

They had a couple of different dorms located mostly within walking distance - there was one or two where you had to take a short bus ride. You can not choose which dorm you will end up in - it is randomly allocated. 
You have to sleep in a room with another student. I lived in a dorm where it is was a small apartment with 6 students in total - this was really nice. From what I heard from others, some of the other dorms where divided into floors instead of apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
At the university the cafeterias serve breakfast, lunch and dinner - which are all really cheap, healthy and good quality food. The price is around 30-35 dkr. 

There is a shared kitchen, but in our kitchen there were no cooking/eating utensils when we moved in. You can always buy cheap pots/pans/plate/etc. in Daiso, but I chose to just eat out every day since it was pretty cheap and really tasty. I went with one of my roomies to eat most of the time, which was really nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Before checking in at the dorm then you need a tubercolusis test (x-ray). It is easist and cheapest to just get it on arrival, where you go to a clinic, where you will be able to get the test done pretty quickly. The dorms will give information about clinics close to the dorm, which can also be found on the dorm website. 

It is not possible to have friends/family in the dorms.

There is a curfew on weekdays from 1-5 am, where it is possible to get into the building, but you will get some penalty points. If you get too many penalty points then they might want you to move out of the dorm - but that is not something you have to worry about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
They send a document throughly explaining the proces of signing up for courses, so I did not find it difficult to sign up for the courses. 

The website where you can look at the different courses is a little difficult to understand, but the websites for signing up for courses are much easier to understand - especially with help from the information documents. 

There are courses meant for exchange students only and then courses where the local students also attend. The courses where the local students attend there might be a certain amount of spaces for exchange students - keep an eye on that since the courses might fill up quickly in the registration period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: they had the information documents, where they explained how to sign up for registration in great detail. The first week of the semester is an add-drop period, where it is possible to switch courses or get more courses. In this week the university personnel are ready to help you + it will also be described in the registration information documents.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the course I wanted since I was ready as the registration opened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend looking into all the courses you want to get and learning their registration system before the registration period. 
If you want to register for a course with few spaces for exchange students then I recommend being ready as the registration opens as to be sure to get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was in general lower that the courses I have taken at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At SKKU it is mostly lectures without exercises thorughout the classes and only few assignments. That also means that I did not have that much time at the school compared to KU. 

I prefer the teaching style at KU, but also found it interesting experiencing another way of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Trade, Advanced Macroeconomic Theory, Labor Economics, Health Economics, Causal Inference for Economists.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend:
Advanced Macroeconomic Theory: It can be transfered as Macroeconomics III at KU and the lecturer in that course was the best I had on exchange. 
Causal Inference for Economists: It is more intuition behind econometrics, which we do not get as much at KU. 
Labor Econ and Health Econ are not that difficult courses - they are nice to see Microeconomics applied to different fields. 

I would not recommend International Trade since it is a 3 hour long lecture, where I do not like the teaching style of the professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a National Health Insurance that you have to pay even if you are insured from home. It is payed each month roughly and is around 350 dkr, I think.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing through the school was relatively inexpensive. 

Eating out every day was also relatively inexpensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a club called Hi-club with the purpose of helping exchange students and holding parties and events for the exchange students. 

In the first week it is possible to sign up for different types of clubs - some being social clubs where exchange students have a chance of meeting and becoming friends with korean students. I regret not signing up in time for these clubs since they seem like a good chance for getting more friends in the beginning - I also got a lot of friends through the hi-club events and my dorm.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the events and activities created by the hi-club and also participating in the ESKARA festival, which is a festival created by the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend travelling within the country to places like: Busan, Jeju, Gyeongju, Sokcho, Gangneung, Jeonju, Gwangju, Nami Island and Suwon. 

I went to all these places during weekends and holidays and felt like I got to see many sides of South Korea there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It is pretty easy to adjust to the local culture since it is not that different from the scandinavian culture. For an example, they eat relatively early and therfore the restaurants close pretty early too. 

The biggest difference is probably that there is so many people all the time wherever you are and that Seoul is a massive city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend participating in the social clubs or the like, if you want to become friends with the korean students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything particularly difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated how much they wanted to share their culture with strangers and eventhough we might not have spoken the same language then they still try to communicate the best they can.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The three most important things I would tell is: have fun, travel the country and make good friends with the othe exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would say that it is pretty tedious and long proces to sign up for exchange, but as soon as you get to go on the exchange then it is really easy and it is so much fun to explore South Korea and see all the different sides of the country. 

Specifically for SKKU they are very good at helping quickly and efficiently with any problem you might have.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was getting to experience living and having a day-to-day in a country pretty different from Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during exchange was getting used to the different teaching style at SKKU compared to at KU.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
